assessment: This paper is of great interest to readers in the fields of vitamin D and obesity. It uses a Mendelian randomization framework to separate the genetically predicted effects of adiposity at two timepoints in the lifecourse, childhood, and adulthood. The key claims are well supported by the data. Higher childhood body size had a direct effect on lower vitamin D levels in early life, while in midlife, childhood body size impacted adult obesity to result in lower vitamin D levels.
